easy.def: The middle part of a wheel.
examples: The spokes meet at the hub.
A bike has a hub in each wheel.
Grease the hub of the wheel.

more.def: The center part of a wheel, or the busy center of an activity or a place where many routes meet.
examples: The spokes of a bicycle wheel all join at the hub.
The big airport is a hub where planes from many cities meet.
The library is the hub of our neighborhood, with something going on every day.

easy.def: A lot of noise from many people.
examples: The hubbub was loud.
A hubbub in the hall.
I heard the hubbub.

more.def: A loud, busy noise made by many people talking or moving at the same time.
examples: The hubbub in the cafeteria was so loud that I could not hear my friend.
A hubbub rose from the crowd when the show began.
We left the hubbub of the city for a quiet walk in the park.

easy.def: A round cover on the middle of a car wheel.
examples: The hubcap fell off.
A shiny hubcap.
The hubcap rolled away.

more.def: A round metal cover on the center of a wheel.
examples: A shiny hubcap rolled down the road.
The car's hubcap came off in the pothole.
He polished the hubcaps on the old car.

easy.def: A small, dark blue berry that grows on a bush.
examples: We picked huckleberries.
The huckleberry is blue.
I saw a huckleberry pie.

more.def: A small, round, dark blue berry that grows wild on low bushes.
examples: We picked huckleberries on the mountain.
Mom baked a huckleberry pie.
Bears love to eat huckleberries.

easy.def: To stand or sit close together.
examples: We huddled in the cold.
The puppies huddle in a pile.
They huddled under one umbrella.

more.def: To crowd close together, usually to keep warm or to talk quietly.
examples: The penguins huddle together to keep warm in the freezing wind.
We huddled under one umbrella in the pouring rain.
The team huddled to plan their next play.

easy.def: A tight group of people.
examples: The team made a huddle.
A huddle of kids stood by the door.
We were in a huddle.

more.def: A small, close group of people, such as a sports team making a plan.
examples: The players gathered in a huddle to talk about the next play.
A huddle of children waited at the bus stop in the cold.
The baby ducks sat in a warm huddle.

easy.def: A color.
examples: The sky had a pink hue.
A bright hue.
The hue of the leaf.

more.def: A color, or a shade of a color.
examples: The sunset painted the sky in hues of pink and orange.
The leaves turned a golden hue in the fall.
The artist mixed paint to get just the right hue of blue.

easy.def: To breathe out hard, or to be cross.
examples: I huffed and puffed.
She huffed and left.
The runner huffed.

more.def: To breathe out loudly, often from effort, or to show you are annoyed.
examples: I huffed and puffed as I ran up the hill.
She huffed and crossed her arms when she lost the game.
The wolf in the story huffed and puffed.

easy.def: Quickly cross.
examples: He was huffy.
A huffy reply.
She sounded huffy.

more.def: Easily upset and likely to show it with a grumpy attitude.
examples: He got huffy when we laughed.
She gave a huffy answer.
The huffy cat walked away.

easy.def: To hold someone close in your arms.
examples: I hug my mom.
Grandma hugged me.
The kids hugged the puppy.

more.def: To put your arms around someone and hold them tight to show love.
examples: She hugged her friend goodbye at the bus stop.
The children hugged each other after the show.
He hugged his teddy bear tightly.

easy.def: A tight hold with your arms around someone.
examples: I gave Dad a hug.
A hug feels warm.
Grandma gave me a big hug.

more.def: The act of holding someone close in your arms to show love.
examples: A warm hug made me feel better.
He gave his sister a big hug at the airport.
Everyone got a hug at the family party.

easy.def: Very big.
examples: A whale is huge.
We saw a huge truck.
I have a huge smile today.

more.def: Extremely large in size or amount.
examples: A huge crowd gathered to watch the parade.
The storm left a huge puddle in the yard.
Winning the award was a huge surprise.

easy.def: Very much.
examples: The show was hugely fun.
He is hugely tall.
She was hugely happy.

more.def: To a very great degree.
examples: The film was hugely popular with children.
The giant pumpkin was hugely heavy.
She was hugely proud of her sister.

easy.def: A Hawaiian dance with swaying hips.
examples: We watched a hula.
She danced the hula.
The hula is graceful.

more.def: A dance from Hawaii in which dancers move their hips and hands to tell a story, often to music.
examples: We watched dancers perform a hula at the luau.
She learned the hula and moved her hands to tell the story of the ocean.
The hula tells stories with graceful moves.

easy.def: A very large, heavy person or thing.
examples: The big boat was a hulk.
A hulk of a bear.
The hulk sat in the harbor.

more.def: A large, heavy thing, such as an old ship or a big, strong person.
examples: The old ship was a rusty hulk in the harbor.
A hulk of a bear lumbered through the woods.
A big hulk of a rock blocked the path.

easy.def: The main body of a ship or boat.
examples: The hull is under the water.
The boat has a wooden hull.
A hole was in the hull.

more.def: The main body of a ship or boat, which floats in the water.
examples: A small crack in the hull let water into the boat.
The hull of the boat was painted blue.
Workers scraped the barnacles off the ship's hull.

easy.def: The hard outside part of a seed or fruit.
examples: Peel the hull off the strawberry.
The hull of the nut is hard.
Take the hull off.

more.def: The outer covering of a seed, nut or fruit, or the small green leaves on a strawberry.
examples: Remove the hull from each strawberry before you eat it.
The hull of the sunflower seed cracked easily.
Birds shell the nuts to get past the tough hull.

easy.def: A big, noisy mess of voices.
examples: There was a hullabaloo.
The hullabaloo was loud.
What a hullabaloo!

more.def: A noisy fuss or uproar.
examples: There was a hullabaloo when the dog got loose.
What is all the hullabaloo about?
The hullabaloo woke up the baby.

easy.def: To sing with your lips closed.
examples: I hum a song.
She hummed while she worked.
Dad hums a tune.

more.def: To make a low, steady sound, or to sing a tune without opening your mouth.
examples: I hummed a tune as I walked.
The bees hummed in the garden.
The refrigerator hums in the kitchen.

easy.def: A person.
examples: Humans have two legs.
A human can use tools.
Dogs are friends of humans.

more.def: A person; a member of the kind of living thing that people belong to.
examples: Humans have been making tools for thousands of years.
The robot looked almost like a human.
Dolphins and humans can both learn from others.

easy.def: Of or about people.
examples: The human body needs water.
Eating is a human need.
A human heart beats all day.

more.def: Of or belonging to people.
examples: Sleeping is a basic human need.
The museum has a model of the human heart.
It is only human to make mistakes.

easy.def: Kind and caring to people and animals.
examples: The vet is humane.
A humane person.
A humane way.

more.def: Showing kindness and care toward people and animals, especially when they are in pain or in need.
examples: The vet is humane and treats every animal gently.
A humane person helps others who are in trouble.
The shelter takes a humane approach to caring for lost pets.

easy.def: All people.
examples: Humanity needs clean water.
The invention helped humanity.
We are all part of humanity.

more.def: All the people of the world, or kindness toward others.
examples: Clean water is important to all of humanity.
The doctor showed great humanity.
The scientist hoped to help humanity.

easy.def: All the people in the world.
examples: Humankind has made many things.
Humankind needs water.
The history of humankind.

more.def: All human beings; people as a whole.
examples: Humankind has built great cities.
Fire changed the life of humankind.
The museum tells the story of humankind.

easy.def: Not bragging.
examples: The winner was humble and kind.
She is humble about her good grades.
The humble boy did not show off.

more.def: Not thinking or acting as if you are better than other people.
examples: Even after winning the prize, she stayed humble.
The humble champion thanked his teammates first.
He gave a humble answer when people praised his work.

easy.def: In a quiet way, without bragging.
examples: She humbly said thank you.
He humbly accepted the prize.
They humbly bowed.

more.def: In a modest way, without bragging.
examples: She humbly accepted the prize and thanked her team.
He humbly said he was just lucky.
The winner humbly bowed to the crowd.

easy.def: A hard mint candy.
examples: Grandpa gave me a humbug.
The humbug was minty.
I sucked on a humbug.

more.def: A hard candy with stripes that tastes like mint.
examples: Grandpa gave me a striped humbug.
The humbug was cool and minty.
A bag of humbugs sat in the dish.

easy.def: Hot and wet in the air.
examples: It is humid today.
The air is humid.
The humid room felt sticky.

more.def: Having a lot of moisture in the air, making it feel sticky.
examples: It was hot and humid at the beach.
The humid air made my hair curl.
Jungles are humid places.

easy.def: How much water is in the air.
examples: The humidity is high.
Humidity makes it sticky.
There is no humidity in the desert.

more.def: The amount of water vapor in the air.
examples: High humidity makes a hot day feel even hotter.
The humidity was so high that our clothes felt damp.
Deserts have very low humidity.

easy.def: To make someone feel very small and ashamed.
examples: Do not humiliate people.
She felt humiliated.
He humiliated her in front of the class.

more.def: To make someone feel foolish or ashamed in front of others.
examples: It is cruel to humiliate someone in front of others.
He felt humiliated when everyone laughed at his mistake.
The boy was humiliated by the mean joke.

easy.def: The sad, red-faced feeling of being laughed at.
examples: He felt humiliation when he dropped his tray.
Her face went red with humiliation.
Nobody wants to feel humiliation at school.

more.def: The feeling of shame you have when something makes you look foolish in front of other people.
examples: He turned red with humiliation when everyone laughed at his mistake.
The coach said teasing causes humiliation and must stop.
She tried to hide her humiliation after tripping on the stage.

easy.def: Not thinking you are better than others.
examples: She showed humility.
He won with humility.
Humility is good.

more.def: The quality of not being proud or boastful, and of seeing that you are not better than other people.
examples: The champion showed humility and thanked everyone who had helped her.
He accepted the prize with humility.
Humility means being able to say, "I do not know everything."

easy.def: A tiny bird that hovers and drinks from flowers.
examples: A hummingbird hovered.
The hummingbird is tiny.
I saw a hummingbird.

more.def: A tiny, brightly colored bird that beats its wings very fast and hovers to drink from flowers.
examples: A hummingbird hovered by the red flower.
The hummingbird's wings beat so fast that they make a humming sound.
The hummingbird sipped from the feeder.

easy.def: Very, very big.
examples: A humongous pizza.
The humongous truck passed.
A humongous wave.

more.def: Extremely big.
examples: We ordered a humongous pizza.
A humongous truck rumbled down the road.
The humongous wave crashed over the rocks.

easy.def: Being funny.
examples: He has a good sense of humor.
The book is full of humor.
I like her humor.

more.def: The quality of being funny, or the ability to see what is funny.
examples: He has a great sense of humor.
The story is full of humor.
A little humor made the lesson fun.

easy.def: Funny and making you laugh.
examples: A humorous story.
The humorous clown.
A humorous song.

more.def: Funny and making people laugh.
examples: The book is a humorous story about a dog who thinks he is a cat.
The clown gave a humorous speech.
She told a humorous tale about her trip.

easy.def: A round bump.
examples: The camel has a hump.
The road has a hump.
The hump is big.

more.def: A round bump on the back of an animal or on the ground.
examples: The camel's hump stores fat.
The car bumped over a hump in the road.
A whale showed its hump above the water.

easy.def: A big whale with a hump on its back.
examples: A humpback jumped.
The humpback is a whale.
We saw a humpback.

more.def: A large whale with a hump on its back and long flippers, known for its songs.
examples: A humpback leaped out of the water.
The humpback sings long, haunting songs.
Humpbacks travel thousands of miles each year.

easy.def: A feeling that something is true without proof.
examples: I have a hunch it will rain.
His hunch was right.
She had a hunch.

more.def: A feeling that you have about something even though you have no proof.
examples: I have a hunch that it will rain tomorrow.
His hunch was right, and he found the key.
She followed her hunch and looked under the bed.

easy.def: To bend your back and shoulders forward.
examples: He hunched over the desk.
She hunched in the cold.
The old man hunched.

more.def: To bend your back and shoulders forward and round.
examples: He hunched over the desk to write.
She hunched her shoulders against the wind.
The cat hunched up in the rain.

easy.def: The number 100.
examples: Count to one hundred.
A hundred kids came to the fair.
She is a hundred years old.

more.def: The number 100, which is ten tens.
examples: A dollar is a hundred cents.
Hundreds of people watched the parade.
The tree is over a hundred years old.

easy.def: Number 100 in a row.
examples: It is the hundredth day of school.
He was the hundredth to arrive.
The hundredth page.

more.def: Coming after ninety-nine others.
examples: Today is the hundredth day of school.
She was the hundredth visitor to the museum.
It was the hundredth time he had read the book.

easy.def: The need for food.
examples: The child felt hunger.
Hunger made her eat fast.
The hunger grew.

more.def: The feeling that you want food, or not having enough food.
examples: Hunger made me eat my lunch fast.
The hikers felt hunger after the climb.
Many groups work to end hunger.

easy.def: In a way that shows you want food.
examples: The puppy ate hungrily.
She hungrily ate lunch.
He looked hungrily at the cake.

more.def: In a way that shows you are hungry, or want something very much.
examples: The hungry puppy gulped down its food hungrily.
She hungrily bit into the sandwich.
The children eyed the cookies hungrily.

easy.def: Wanting food.
examples: I am hungry for lunch.
The hungry baby cried.
Are you hungry for a snack?

more.def: Feeling that you need or want to eat.
examples: The hungry kittens meowed until they were fed.
After the long hike, we were all hungry.
The hungry birds gathered at the feeder.

easy.def: To squat down low.
examples: The cat hunkered down.
We hunkered down in the storm.
He hunkered by the fire.

more.def: To crouch down low, or to settle in a safe place and stay there.
examples: The campers hunkered down in their tent during the storm.
The cat hunkered low in the grass.
We hunkered by the fire to keep warm.

easy.def: To look for something.
examples: We hunt for shells.
She hunted for her shoe.
I hunt for eggs.

more.def: To search for something.
examples: We hunted for seashells on the beach.
She hunted for her missing shoe.
The kids hunt for eggs at Easter.

easy.def: To chase and catch animals for food.
examples: Owls hunt at night.
Lions hunt for food.
Wolves hunt in packs.

more.def: To chase and kill wild animals for food or sport.
examples: Owls hunt mice at night.
Lions hunt together to catch zebras.
Long ago, people hunted to feed their families.

easy.def: A person or animal that looks for animals to catch for food.
examples: The hunter walked in the woods.
A fox is a hunter.
The owl is a night hunter.

more.def: A person or animal that chases and catches other animals for food.
examples: The lion is a skilled hunter on the grassy plains.
The hunter followed the tracks through the snow.
Owls are hunters that listen carefully for mice.

easy.def: Looking for animals to catch for food.
examples: Wolves go hunting at night.
The owl does its hunting after dark.
Cats like hunting.

more.def: The act of looking for and catching animals for food.
examples: Wolves do their hunting at night.
The eagle spotted a mouse while hunting.
Long ago, people lived by hunting and gathering.

easy.def: A woman who hunts.
examples: The huntress followed the trail.
A huntress used a bow.
The huntress was brave.

more.def: A woman who hunts animals, especially in old stories.
examples: The huntress followed the trail into the woods.
In the myth, the huntress carried a silver bow.
The huntress walked quietly through the forest.

easy.def: A man who hunts.
examples: The huntsman went in the woods.
The huntsman had a horn.
A huntsman walked with dogs.

more.def: A man who hunts animals, especially in old stories.
examples: The huntsman followed the deer into the woods.
In the old tale, the huntsman saved the girl.
A huntsman blew his horn to call his dogs.

easy.def: A low fence that runners jump over.
examples: She jumped over the hurdle.
Runners jump the hurdle.
The hurdle is low.

more.def: A low barrier that runners jump over in a race, or a problem that is hard to get past.
examples: The runner leaped over each hurdle in the race.
Learning to read was a big hurdle, but she did it.
The team cleared one more hurdle on the way to the finals.

easy.def: To throw something hard.
examples: He hurled the ball.
She hurled a rock into the lake.
The pitcher hurled the ball.

more.def: To throw something with great force, especially as far as you can.
examples: He hurled the ball across the field as hard as he could.
The pitcher hurled a fast pitch to home plate.
She hurled a stone into the lake and watched the splash.

easy.def: A shout of joy.
examples: Hurrah! We won!
Hurrah for the team!
They shouted hurrah.

more.def: A shout of joy or praise when something good happens.
examples: "Hurrah!" the crowd cried when the team scored the winning goal.
Hurrah for the cook who made this wonderful dinner!
We all gave a loud hurrah as the ship pulled into the harbor.

easy.def: A shout of joy.
examples: Hurray! We won!
Hooray for the team!
She shouted hurray.

more.def: A shout of happiness or praise when something good happens.
examples: Hurray! The sun is out at last.
The children shouted "hooray" when school ended.
Hurray for the cook who made this meal!

easy.def: A very big storm with strong wind and lots of rain.
examples: The hurricane knocked down trees.
We stayed inside in the hurricane.
A hurricane brings big waves.

more.def: A huge, powerful storm with very strong winds and heavy rain that forms over the ocean.
examples: People boarded up their windows before the hurricane arrived.
The hurricane flooded streets near the coast.
Weather experts tracked the hurricane as it crossed the sea.

easy.def: In a fast way because there is not much time.
examples: She hurriedly ate her lunch.
I hurriedly packed my bag.
He hurriedly ran to class.

more.def: Done in a quick way, because you do not have much time.
examples: They hurriedly packed their bags before the bus came.
She hurriedly finished her homework before dinner.
The boy hurriedly put on his coat and ran for the door.

easy.def: To move or do something fast.
examples: Hurry, or we will be late!
I hurried to the door.
We hurry to catch the bus.

more.def: To move or act quickly because there is not much time.
examples: We hurried to the station so we would not miss the train.
Hurry up, or the ice cream will melt!
She hurried through her homework so she could go outside.

easy.def: A need to be fast.
examples: I am in a hurry.
Why are you in such a hurry?
Dad was in a hurry.

more.def: A need to do something quickly because time is short.
examples: In her hurry, she forgot her lunch box.
There is no hurry, so take your time.
He ran out the door in a hurry.

easy.def: To cause pain.
examples: My knee hurts.
I hurt my arm.
Do not hurt the cat.

more.def: To cause pain or an injury, or to feel pain.
examples: I fell and hurt my knee on the pavement.
Does your tooth still hurt?
Her words hurt his feelings.

easy.def: Feeling pain or sore.
examples: I am hurt.
The hurt dog limps.
She felt hurt.

more.def: Feeling pain in the body, or feeling upset.
examples: The hurt bird could not fly until its wing healed.
He felt hurt when his friend forgot his birthday.
The nurse helped the hurt child.

easy.def: Saying or doing things that make people sad.
examples: That was a hurtful thing to say.
His words were hurtful.
The hurtful joke made her cry.

more.def: Causing pain, especially to someone's feelings.
examples: That was a hurtful thing to say to your friend.
His hurtful words made her sad.
She said sorry for her hurtful joke.

easy.def: To move very fast.
examples: The train will hurtle by.
The ball hurtled past.
The car hurtled down the hill.

more.def: To move or rush with great speed and force.
examples: The train hurtled through the station.
The ball hurtled across the field.
The sled hurtled down the snowy hill.

easy.def: A man who is married to someone.
examples: Aunt Rosa's husband drives a bus.
Her husband bakes bread on Sundays.
Is he your friend's husband?

more.def: A married man, when you are talking about the person he is married to.
examples: The author thanked her husband for reading her stories first.
The two sisters and their husbands went camping together.
My neighbor and her husband planted a big vegetable garden.

easy.def: To be quiet.
examples: Hush, the baby is asleep.
She hushed the crowd.
The class hushed.

more.def: To make someone be quiet, or to become quiet.
examples: Hush, the baby is sleeping.
The teacher hushed the class.
The crowd hushed as the show began.

easy.def: Quiet.
examples: The hushed room.
In a hushed voice.
The hushed crowd waited.

more.def: Very quiet and calm.
examples: They talked in hushed voices.
A hushed crowd waited for the singer.
The room was hushed when the teacher entered.

easy.def: The dry outside covering of corn or seeds.
examples: Peel the husk off the corn.
The husk is dry.
A husk covers the corn.

more.def: The dry outer covering of some seeds and fruits, such as corn.
examples: Peel the husk off the ear of corn.
The husks were dry and rough.
A husk covered each grain of rice.

easy.def: In a low, rough voice.
examples: He spoke huskily.
She whispered huskily.
The singer sang huskily.

more.def: In a low, rough, hoarse voice.
examples: He spoke huskily because of his cold.
The singer sang huskily into the microphone.
"Hello," she whispered huskily.

easy.def: Big and strong, or rough-sounding.
examples: A husky man.
His voice was husky.
A husky boy.

more.def: Big and strong in build, or having a rough, low voice.
examples: The husky man lifted the heavy box with ease.
His voice was husky because he had a cold.
She is a husky player on the football team.

easy.def: A strong dog with thick fur that pulls sleds.
examples: The husky pulled the sled.
Huskies have thick fur.
A husky in the snow.

more.def: A strong dog with thick fur that is used to pull sleds across snow.
examples: A team of huskies pulled the sled across the snow.
The husky's thick fur kept it warm in the arctic cold.
Huskies like to run and howl.

easy.def: To hurry.
examples: We hustle to the bus.
The kids hustled to class.
Hustle up!

more.def: To move or work quickly.
examples: The kids hustled to catch the bus.
He hustled down the hall.
Hustle up, or we will be late.

easy.def: A small, simple house.
examples: The hut is made of mud.
They lived in a hut.
The hut has one room.

more.def: A very small, plain house, often made from wood, mud or grass.
examples: The hut had a roof made of grass.
The shepherd slept in a hut.
We built a hut in the woods.

easy.def: A small cage or house for a pet rabbit.
examples: The rabbit is in the hutch.
The hutch has a door.
I clean the hutch.

more.def: A small box-like house or cage for a rabbit or other small animal.
examples: The rabbit hopped into its hutch for the night.
We built a wooden hutch for the guinea pig.
The hutch has a wire door and a warm bed of straw.
